About

Research that businesses can actually use

I'm Esther Daramola, a market research analyst focused on turning raw data and consumer behavior into insight businesses can act on.

My work sits at the intersection of market research, competitor analysis, business research, product research, and data analysis — helping businesses answer the questions that shape real decisions: who their customer is, where the market is moving, and how they stack up against competitors.

I approach every project the same way: understand the business question first, then choose the research method that actually answers it — not the other way around.

Specialization Areas

  • Consumer & Market Research
  • Competitive Intelligence & Benchmarking
  • Business & Feasibility Research
  • Product Research & Validation
  • Data Analysis & Insight Reporting

Pickle Park & Pub — Business & Market Research

Business and market research for a proposed indoor pickleball and recreational venue, built into a full business plan.

Market SizingIndustry ResearchFinancial Modeling
The problemIdentified a shortage of accessible, well-maintained indoor pickleball courts against one of the fastest-growing sports in the U.S.
The researchSized the opportunity across the pickleball, recreation, and health & fitness markets and translated it into a five-year financial model, including NPV and payback period.
The outcomeDefined measurable objectives spanning customer experience, facility utilization, community partnerships, and a phased expansion plan.

U.S. Consumable Bottled Water Industry — Feasibility Study

A market research feasibility study on the U.S. bottled water industry, covering segments, target audiences, and openings for new entrants.

Industry ClassificationConsumer SegmentsFeasibility Study
The marketMapped the industry across still, sparkling, flavored, alkaline, canned, and boxed water, using official NAICS industry classifications as the research base.
The opportunityIdentified openings for new entrants in functional and sustainably packaged water, backed by shifting consumer habits away from soda.
The audienceDefined four target consumer groups — health-conscious millennials, busy professionals, eco-conscious consumers, and the fitness community.
